title: PostgreSQL Disaster Post-Mortem: Dropped Table Recovery Without Backup Restore
realWorldScenario: At 15:00 UTC, an engineer intending to drop a staging table accidentally executes `DROP TABLE payments;` on the production database. The database is 4 Terabytes. Restoring from yesterday's full backup would take 8 hours and lose 15 hours of business transactions.
questionStatement: Architect an emergency disaster recovery plan to recover the dropped `payments` table with zero lost data and minimum downtime. Detail Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR) to a temporary clone instance, `pg_dump` extraction of the single table, and selective re-import into production.

symptoms: 4 TB database; full restore would take 8+ hours
Ongoing writes occurring on remaining tables (orders, customers)
Immediate recovery needed without rolling back other tables

systemTelemetry.logSnippet:
2026-11-01 15:00:02 UTC [4901]: [1-1] LOG:  statement: DROP TABLE payments;
2026-11-01 15:00:03 UTC [4901]: [2-1] LOG:  duration: 120.452 ms

candidateTasks: Do NOT restore full database over live production (would wipe 15 hours of other tables)
Spin up an isolated recovery instance from latest base backup and WAL archive
Set recovery_target_time to 14:59:59 UTC (1 second before DROP TABLE)
Extract single table using pg_dump -t payments and restore to live production

expectedConcepts: Never rolling back production cluster over live unrelated tables
Spinning up isolated temporary instance from base backup
Configuring recovery_target_time to exact second before DROP TABLE
pg_dump -t payments single-table extraction in custom format
hints: Why would restoring the full database to 14:59 lose all other data generated since then?
How does setting recovery_target_time stop replay right before the DROP command in WAL?
Use pg_dump -t to extract only the single missing table.
